caveats.summary: eCFR lists only agencies that have a chapter in the Code of Federal Regulations. For a non-regulatory or non-executive body, having no CFR chapter is correct rather than opaque, and is recorded as NOT_APPLICABLE rather than ABSENT.

The Federal Register agency list covers bodies that submit documents for publication in the Federal Register. It retains defunct agencies as first-class entries and carries no active/abolished flag, so the absence of an agency is ambiguous and its presence does not imply it still exists.

PLUM omits at least 7 federal entities and at least 130 Senate-confirmed positions, and contains inconsistent identifiers and duplicate positions. OPM concurred with all recommendations. Absence from PLUM is therefore evidence of a gap in PLUM, not proof that an agency has no such positions.

description.value:
The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) was created in the wake of 9/11 to strengthen the security of the nation’s transportation systems while ensuring the freedom of movement for people and commerce. Originally established as a subagency of  the Department of Transportation, TSA was transferred to the Department of Homeland Security in March of 2003.

In March 2003, TSA transferred from the Department of Transportation to the Department of Homeland Security.

TSA employs a risk-based strategy to secure U.S. transportation systems, working closely with stakeholders in aviation, rail, transit, highway, and pipeline sectors, as well as the partners in the law enforcement and intelligence community. The agency will continuously set the standard for excellence in transportation security through its people, processes, technologies and use of intelligence to drive operations.
